recipes.name: Cheesy Buffalo Chicken Dip
ingredients_raw: 0.33333334326744 cup hot pepper sauce (such as Frank's RedHot®)

steps.text: Place chicken breasts in a large saucepan; cover with water. Bring to a boil and cook until no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, about 20 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of a breast should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Drain and allow chicken to cool enough to handle. Pull meat from bones and skin. Shred meat and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir celery in hot oil until soft. Mix in cream cheese, blue cheese dressing, and ranch dressing. Cook and stir until smooth and creamy. Stir in shredded chicken and hot sauce. Transfer to an 8x8-inch baking dish and sprinkle with shredded cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden and bubbly, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheesy Buffalo Chicken Dip
raw_recipe.description: This Buffalo shredded chicken dip features a tasty blend of ranch and blue cheese dressings for a hot, cheesy, flavorful appetizer served with chips.

video.description:
This hot dip is perfect for a tailgate party or a yummy snack! Blue cheese 
dressing and ranch blend to make a rich, tangy flavor that pairs well 
with hot pepper sauce. Shredded chicken, cream cheese, hot sauce 
and lots of melted cheese create a wonderful buffalo wing flavor!

review.reviewBody: I love this dip! I made a few changes: I used 2 cans of chicken (12.5 oz each), 2 stalks of celery finely chopped, I didn't use blue cheese or ranch dressing instead I used 1 16oz container of sour cream and a packet of ranch dip seasoning and made the ranch dip. I added it all to the mix. The ranch dip has a better taste than the dressing to me. All in all the dip was a hit at girls night....they are already asking me to make it for our next get together :)

First time I made it I was happy with the flavor but not the consistency, so this time instead of regular cheddar, I used Cabot American cheese slices, and it came out like from a local restaurant known for a similar dip. I also skipped the oven and just melted everything on the stove top.

Excellent! We did a few things differently: 5 bone-in chicken breasts were put in the crock pot and we doubled the recipe except for using the same amount of ranch and blue cheese dressing as the recipe calls for (we didn't want it to be too soupy from making it in the crockpot). We used Moore's Buffalo wing sauce and Frank's Red Hot Wings Buffalo sauce. (We did double the total amount of wing sauce but only maybe 1/4 of that was the Frank's sauce because we didn't want it to be too hot). We also put a 6oz can of diced green chiles in and then chopped up some celery and put it on top with some additional Frank's drizzle. Oh, we also added some blue cheese crumbles in, maybe a 1/4 cup. Delicious- everyone raved about it and it wasn't greasy when we reheated the little bit we had left the next day.

This is one of our favorites! I also made a few changes. I used one 12.5oz can of chicken (but next time will probably use two cans) one doesn't seem quite enough. Even one & a half would be good. 3/4 cup of RedHot sauce, if you don't like spicy food I would make it 1/2 cup. Two 8oz blocks of cream cheese, softened. 1 cup ranch dressing. And about 1&1/4 cups sharp cheddar cheese, because we love cheese! This is actually really quick and easy. I bake dish for 15 mins, take out and add the cheese evenly, and put back in the oven for 10 or 15 minutes. Prep time 5-7 mins, bake 25-30 mins, & enjoy!!!

I liked it and more importantly....It was a hit w my coworkers.... I doubled the recipe and used boneless chicken breast... instead of 2 cups of cheddar I used 1 cup of cheddar and 1 cup of pepper jack... and used a little more than 2/3 Cup of hot sauce.. just by taste... and I did not top w shredded cheese before baking... I mixed in the shredded cheeses... delish!

I made this recipe for NYE and it was a hit! I used the exact measurement of ranch and blue cheese dressing and 1-8oz countainer of regular cream cheese. I used 1/2 cup of Franks Buffalo Wingsauce (because less than that is not enough to compete with the amount of dressing imo). And I used a 48oz package of boneless skinless chicken breast. It could have actually used a little more meat than that just to soak up some more of the dressing-cream cheese mixture, I think. I mixed the cream cheese and dressing together and the chicken and wingsauce together and then mixed them all together. Then, I put them in my 8x8 dish with the cup of shredded cheese on top. I put it in the oven for 25 minutes and then I just turned the broiler on high for less than five minutes and that really got the cheese on top a golden color. I think the broiler helped a lot with that layer of grease that I have seen other people mention, because when I took it out of the oven, I had only a very thin layer of grease to blot up. The people at the party (there were only 7 of us) destroyed that dip with Fritos scoops. My husband kept saying he wanted to wrap it up in tortillas. Also, I think it is important to use the full flavor dressings and cream cheese so that it is not too runny. I think that may be the problem some people here had who are saying their's came out too runny (and maybe they did not use enough chicken). Will make this again!

Every time I make cheesy buffalo chicken dip and take it to family functions I always leave with an empty crockpot! I always put 50% more cheese in than it calls for because we all love cheese! I pour it all into a crock pot, add half the cheese, mix it in then top with the rest of the cheese. Then I throw the crock into the oven to bake! Come out awesomeness! Then it's easy to keep warm at the function! Happy cooking!

Followed others advice and used rotisserie chicken chopped, 1/2 pkg cream cheese, 2 T sour cream, 1/2 pkg ranch, some diced onions since that's what I had in the pantry. I also didn't realize we were out of Franks so I used some texas pete and melted butter into it. 

Mixed cream cheese, sour cream and ranch mix together, added hot sauce to the chicken, then cream cheese mixture and onions, mixed everything together and then put into casserole dish lined in aluminum foil, topped w/shredded cheddar and cooked until bubbily. Served with Tostitos Scoops they were awesome!

I made this dip for Super Bowl Sunday and it was a big hit!! I doubled the recipe and cooked the chicken breast in my electric pressure cooker with some Franks Hot Sauce, Garlic, Onions, and water. The breast were falling apart when I pulled them out and then took a fork to finish them up. Everyone LOVE IT!! I will make this again!

I use 4 bone in chicken breasts. I boil them until tender and falling off the bone. I shred and cut the meat off the bone. I like a lot of celery. I use a full bunch of celery. I cut each stalk in half lengthwise, then chop the stalks up. Sauté the celery in olive oil, while the chicken is cooking, until wilted and tender. Follow the rest of the recipe as is. This always gets tons of compliments! Yum!

This was a hit! I actually bought yogurt dressing my accident and it came delicious and probably healthier! Be liberal with the hot sauce. I used 3/4 cup franks but a cup would have been fine! I also added a few shakes of Louisiana hot sauce. 

Like other reviewers I also used boneless chicken breasts. I poached in herbs and shredded about 4 breasts. Yum!
Love this recipe!! Only change is I 1/2 the hot sauce. Everything else I follow to the letter! Family favorite. 💝

I’ve made this for several years now. My only substitution(s) were as followed. 1. Changed out celery for Ro*tel crushed tomatoes with habanero peppers. This also eliminates the hot sauce, whew! 🌶️ spicy. 2. Instead of 2/3 cup of Ranch dressing, I mixed 1/3 Ranch and 1/3 Creamy Garlic dressing? Why did I do this? Because I had it all on hand. Be careful if you choose the Ro*tel with habanero peppers. If you’re not careful, it could be too spicy for your taste. Overall, this is a keeper. I’ve been making this for several years now. Always a crowd pleaser. Enjoy 😊

I already knew I loved it. It was getting my picky sister to try it LOL due to there being hot sauce in it; well it is safe to say, she ate more than anyone else did, she loved it as much as I did. Next time I make it, it looks like I will have to double the recipe :-)
Excellent! I used about double the hot sauce because I like a little more heat. Extra cheesy. Great taste. It freezes well in case you need to. Keto friendly with celery sticks.
Very easy! It turned out great with fantastic taste!
